title: Serial Monitor & Debugging
summary: Learn to talk to your computer with Serial.begin and Serial.println.

steps.title: What is Serial Communication?
steps.markdownContent:
Your Arduino board and computer can talk to each other over the USB cable using **Serial communication**. They send text messages back and forth, one bit at a time (serially).

This is incredibly useful! You can use it to send commands to the robot or have the robot tell you sensor values. The IDE has a built-in tool called the **Serial Monitor** (under the Tools menu) to view these messages.

quickCheck.question: What is the Serial Monitor in the Arduino IDE used for?
options: Viewing diagnostic messages, text outputs, and sensor readings sent from the board
quickCheck.explanation: The Serial Monitor lets the Arduino "speak" to your computer screen using Serial.println()!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: If your robot can't talk out loud yet, it sends text messages to the Serial Monitor.

quickCheck.question: What command initializes Serial communication at a speed of 9600 baud in setup()?
quickCheck.explanation: Serial.begin(9600); wakes up the serial hardware and sets the baud rate to 9600 bits per second!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Serial.begin(9600) opens the telephone line so your Arduino can talk to your screen.

steps.title: Baud Rate Mismatch
steps.markdownContent:
What happens if the baud rate in `Serial.begin(9600)` doesn't match the dropdown in the Serial Monitor? 

You get garbage characters like `⸮⸮⸮`. See what happens in the demo below when the speeds don't match.

interactiveConfig.question: What does Serial.begin() do?
interactiveConfig.explanation: Serial.begin() prepares the hardware UART to send and receive text at a specific speed.

questions.question: What does Serial.begin() do?
questions.explanation: Serial.begin() prepares the hardware UART to send and receive text at a specific speed.

questions.question: Why do we use Serial.println()?
options: To print text and variables for debugging
To make the code run faster
questions.explanation: It sends readable text to the computer so you can see what the Arduino is doing inside.

questions.question: What happens if the baud rate on the computer doesn't match the Arduino?
options: You see garbage characters (gibberish) instead of text
questions.explanation: If the two devices expect different bit speeds, the text is interpreted incorrectly.
